transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 14:00 EST
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood Sec), Samantha (Millbrook CISO), Marcus (Millbrook Cloud), Priya (Product), Donovan (Compliance)

Summary: Short discovery focused on data residency, logging restrictions for regulated banking data, and the tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Customer wants to confirm whether Redwood Hosted can meet EU/UK data residency requirements and HIPAA/FSI controls, and what gaps remain vs Dedicated/Private.

Topics:
- Data residency (EU/UK/US segmentation)
- Logging, retention, and redaction controls
- SOC2/ISO/HIPAA evidence and KMS/HSM controls
- Network connectivity (VPC peering / private links)
- Performance and pilot/benchmark approach

[00:00] Jamie Clarke: Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to meet you all. quick roll call?
[00:08] Samantha Lee: Hey Samantha here, CISO at Millbrook. we've got Marcus on infra, Priya on product and Donovan from compliance.
[00:15] Marcus Bell: Marcus, thank you.
[00:18] Jamie Clarke: Awesome. I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood, and Arjun is our SE and Leah is on security. We'll keep this high level then dive into compliance questions.
[00:28] Arjun Patel: hi all, thanks for the time. we'll try to capture requirements and match them to Hosted, Dedicated, Private options.

[00:40] Samantha Lee: high level: Millbrook is rolling out an internal agent for customer support that may surface account numbers and limited PHI in support scenarios. regulatory requirement is data residency — EU data stays in EU, UK data in UK, and some US PII cannot leave the country; also strict audit logging and log retention controls, minimum 7 years for some records.
[01:05] Jamie Clarke: got it. for residency, our Hosted API offers region pins for requests and we have EU/UK/US regions. question is whether logs or any customer payloads persist outside pinned regions. Arjun, quick take?
[01:18] Arjun Patel: yes, on Hosted we persist telemetry and some diagnostics to the region but there are caveats: metadata and aggregated metrics might be processed in our global observability stack. for customers with strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control where logs land and optionally disable telemetry.
[01:35] Samantha Lee: are those aggregated metrics considered customer data? we have internal counsel that treats even aggregated request metadata as PII in context.
[01:42] Leah Ramos: short answer: depends. we classify what we store as request payloads, KV cache, and logs. in Hosted we retain request transcripts for a configurable window for debugging — we can reduce that and offer redaction hooks, but for absolute residency guarantees customers go Dedicated or Private.

[02:05] Marcus Bell: network wise we need a VPC private link — we can't have egress over public internet for certain flows. does Redwood offer VPC peering or private link to Dedicated?
[02:15] Jamie Clarke: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering/private connectivity and Private deployment is customer-managed in their VPC or on-prem. Hosted supports regional endpoints but not direct VPC peering.
[02:26] Samantha Lee: HIPAA question: the support agent might occasionally surface PHI. is Redwood willing to sign a BAA for Hosted? Dedicated? Private?
[02:35] Leah Ramos: we can sign BAA for Private deployments generally; Hosted BAAs are evaluated case-by-case — the default Hosted product doesn't include a BAA. Dedicated often sits in the middle — for some customers we've executed BAAs on Dedicated with additional contractual controls and logical isolation.

[02:54] Priya Nair: what's the difference in cost and perf between Dedicated and Private? we want sub-200ms token latency for chat in peak hours.
[03:02] Arjun Patel: Dedicated is our reserved pool — we manage the control plane but you get isolated GPU capacity. Private is fully customer-managed, so you own infra ops. Performance for both can meet sub-200ms depending on model choice and instance types; Private gives you more headroom to tune kernels, but requires your ops team to manage autoscaling.

[03:28] Donovan Reed: audit logs are big for us. we need immutable audit trails, retention for 7 years, and the ability to produce logs on demand for regulators. does Redwood provide WORM-like retention?
[03:40] Leah Ramos: Hosted does not currently provide guaranteed WORM retention. We have append-only audit logs with retention windows, and we can export logs to the customer's S3 or customer-managed storage for long-term archival on Dedicated/Private. that's the recommended pattern.

[03:58] Samantha Lee: encryption: we need customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest and HSM-backed keys for certain vaulted data.
[04:07] Jamie Clarke: we integrate with KMS; Hosted supports provider-managed keys by default, but Dedicated and Private support customer-supplied KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and key wrapping.

[04:20] Marcus Bell: what about telemetry: request traces, slow request sampling — these often include prompts and partial responses. can we opt out?
[04:28] Arjun Patel: yes you can disable storing full transcripts on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has sampling and you can request redaction. for strict cases we recommend turning off transcript storage and use local prefix caching to preserve perf without storing text.

[04:50] Samantha Lee: GDPR DSARs and right to erasure — if a customer requests deletion, how does data flow in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[05:00] Leah Ramos: Hosted: we have deletion APIs and can fulfill erasure requests, but again some aggregated logs may persist per backup/retention; we can coordinate deletions. Dedicated: easier to scope and delete since you have isolated storage; Private: you control everything. for GDPR-sensitive workloads we typically advise Dedicated with contractual commitments or Private if they must guarantee physical locality.

[05:25] Priya Nair: timeline: we're aiming to run a 6-week pilot and then production by Q3. what would you recommend as a pilot approach?
[05:33] Arjun Patel: common pattern: start with Hosted in the target region to validate models and UX, while concurrently standing up a Dedicated proof of concept for residency and logging verification. run a focused benchmark (throughput, p95 latency, cost per token) on Dedicated. if strict controls still unsatisfied, move to Private.

[05:55] Marcus Bell: for the benchmark, will Redwood run it in our environment or you need access to our infra?
[06:01] Arjun Patel: for Dedicated we can provision a sandbox in our environment with isolated capacity; for Private we run benchmarks in your infra — we'll provide an infra runbook and sample workload.

[06:14] Samantha Lee: what compliance artifacts can you share now? SOC2, ISO27001, penetration test reports?
[06:21] Leah Ramos: we'll share SOC2 Type II summary, ISO attestations, and redacted pen test summaries under NDA. Jamie will drop those docs after the call.

[06:35] Donovan Reed: logging: we need the ability to redact sensitive fields before logs leave our VPC. do you have built-in pre-request hooks or can we run a filter?
[06:43] Arjun Patel: Dedicated supports pre-ingest redaction and middleware filters; Private gives you full control. Hosted supports a pre-send SDK hook for redaction but it requires you to implement client-side filtering.

[06:58] Samantha Lee: regulatory nuance: some regulators require auditability of the model decisioning — they want to see prompts, outputs, and any system flags. how do you reconcile that with redaction needs?
[07:08] Leah Ramos: we usually do a separation: keep a redacted operational log for production usage, and a secured, access-controlled forensic log store for regulator requests. that forensic store is typically on customer-managed storage in Dedicated/Private. access is gated with RBAC and just-in-time access controls.

[07:35] Jamie Clarke: quick note on roadmap: we're rolling out more fine-grained retention and region-scoped telemetry in the next quarter, which may help Hosted customers. will share ETA in the follow-up.

[07:48] Priya Nair: are there any documented case studies for banks that went Dedicated/Private for residency?
[07:54] Jamie Clarke: yes, we have redacted case studies and a reference architecture for banks. I'll include links in the follow-up.

[08:05] Samantha Lee: ok final items for us: 1) we need to see SOC2/ISO docs; 2) an architecture doc showing where logs land for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; 3) a proposed pilot plan with timelines and who from Redwood will execute benchmarks; 4) pricing estimate for Dedicated pilot.
[08:22] Jamie Clarke: got it — we'll get those over. Arjun will run the technical deep dive and benchmark.

[08:34] Jamie Clarke: any final questions?
[08:37] Marcus Bell: one more — data residency: is there any case where Hosted replicates data outside pinned region for redundancy?
[08:44] Leah Ramos: for failover we have cross-region backups for some services; we can either opt out of cross-region backups on Dedicated/Private or encrypt them with customer keys such that only you can decrypt if they're replicated. we'll detail specifics in doc.

[09:02] Samantha Lee: thank you, that's helpful. we'll review and come back with the pilot scope.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Jamie to send SOC2, ISO, GDPR mapping, redacted pen test summary, and case studies (by 2026-03-06)
- Arjun to schedule technical deep dive and provide Dedicated pilot config + benchmark runbook (by 2026-03-09)

Action items captured above. Meeting ends.
